The build-up 2021 – 2024 · World Cup awarded; the PA enters government
November 2021
International Cricket Council (ICC) announces South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia as co-hosts for 2027 Men’s Cricket World Cup.
March 2023
Astrid Harrison wears Patriotic Alliance (PA) t-shirt in Facebook post, says she is a “proud, disciplined member” of the party.
May 2024
South Africa holds general elections. Gayton McKenzie’s PA wins nine seats in parliament.
June 2024
The PA agrees to join the ANC-led Government of National Unity (GNU).
The appointments 2024 · McKenzie’s first months as sport minister
July 2024
President Cyril Ramaphosa appoints McKenzie as Minister of Sport, Arts and Culture. Bakang Lethoko becomes McKenzie’s Chief of Staff.
Gayton McKenzie
Bakang Lethoko
July 2024
Omphemetse Mokgosi appointed to the board of Johannesburg Roads Agency (JRA). The JRA is controlled by Kenny Kunene, the City of Johannesburg’s MMC for Transport and the PA’s deputy president.
Omphemetse Mokgosi
August 2024
Astrid Harrison’s husband, Timothy, becomes director of the newly-established Spinning Sport South Africa.
October 2024
R5m
McKenzie’s department announces R5-million in funding for Spinning Sport South Africa.
November 2024
McKenzie appoints Omphemetse Mokgosi to the board of the National Film and Video Foundation (NFVF).
Omphemetse Mokgosi
December 2024
McKenzie appoints Bakang Lethoko as chairperson for new Formula One Bid Steering Committee.
Bakang Lethoko
The sale 2024 – 2027 · Ticketpro changes hands before the World Cup
Date TBC
JSE-listed Blu Label Unlimited enters negotiations to sell Blu Label subsidiary Ticketpro to a women-owned empowerment consortium.
May 2026
Blu Label sells Ticketpro to women-owned empowerment consortium.
1 June 2026
Blu Label executives Brandon Duffield, Deelan Rama and Kavir Kistnasamy resign as directors of Ticketpro. McKenzie associate Bakang Lethoko steps in as Ticketpro’s sole director.
Bakang Lethoko
20 August 2026
A new company, Ticketpro Group, is registered. The directors are PA-linked Astrid Harrison and Omphemetse Mokgosi, together with media and advertising professional Zanele Dube.
Astrid Harrison
Omphemetse Mokgosi
Zanele Dube
October – November 2027
ICC Cricket World Cup to be hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia.
